title: Creational, structural and behavioural patterns (GoF) in practice

videos.script: In 1994 four authors published a catalogue of twenty-three designs. They kept turning up in good object-oriented code, so the book gave each one a name. {{book}} Thirty years on, those names are still how developers talk about structure. Say adapter, or strategy, and a colleague sees the shape at once. {{names}} This lesson works through thirteen of them, in pairs that are easy to confuse. Factory and builder. Adapter and facade. Decorator and proxy. {{pairs}} Each pair is a small program about the library. Fines that stack rules like layers. {{fines}} A copy of a book that refuses a loan while it is held for somebody else. {{copy}} A desk that can undo its last three actions. {{undo}} One pattern gets a section of warnings. The singleton is famous, and it is a global variable with a respectable name. {{singleton}} The lesson ends with a question the book could not ask in 1994. What happens to a pattern when the language already does its job? In Python, several of them shrink to a single line. {{language}}
